newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech crown steadies after cen bank repo rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Czech crown steadies after cen bank repo rate rise.

text.p: The Czech central bank, as expected, raised another one of its key rates on Monday, its repo rate, steadying the beleaguered crown.
After raising its Lombard rate on Friday to 50 percent from a previous 14 percent, the CNB held three repo tenders all at a maximum rate of 45 percent, up from 12.9 percent on Friday.

The moves appeared to hit their mark with the crown steadying at about 2.8 percent below the mid-point of the central bank's mark/dollar basket by midday after trading between -2.9 to -3.1 ahead of the rate rise and 3.8 percent on Friday.
Dealers said the crown should remain steady for the coming days, though sentiment on the market had not changed.

"Right now it looks fine, I don't expect any big changes in the crown rate," said one local trader. "But the solutions were only for the short-term, the central bank must follow up if it wants peace for the crown."
The CNB fixed the crown at 30.548 against the dollar and at 18.026 to the mark on Monday, implying a deviation of 2.7 percent below basket parity, after -3.8 percent on Friday.

Last week the crown fell below the five percent level of its basket parity, prompting the CNB to intervene on the market for the first time in over a year. But this failed to stem the tide of bearish sentiment against the crown, forcing the central bank to raise rates late on Friday.

The CNB has said the crown's fall was due to fluctuations of several foreign currencies. It did not elaborate, but some traders said foreign investors were getting nervous over some emerging market economies troubled by a weak external position, such as Thailand.
